questions.stem: Why can the body not simply store excess amino acids?

options.text: Because amino acids dissolve in water and are lost in sweat
Because amino acids are too large to fit inside cells
Because the body has no way to store excess proteins or amino acids
Because excess amino acids are converted to glucose automatically

questions.explanation: Unlike glucose (stored as glycogen) or fats, the body cannot store excess amino acids or proteins. This is why excess amino acids must be deaminated in the liver, producing urea as a waste product.
